findings.doc_says: The commands are not one-per-skill... /docs-update reaches both.
findings.code_says: /docs-init also conditionally activates the `adr` skill and binds $ADR_DIR when it creates docs/dev/README.md from the template (module/commands/docs-init.md:26-31, 77-79), so /docs-update is not the only command that reaches both skills.

findings.doc_says: Three IPv6 ranges get handling beyond that: ::/96 + fec0::/10, 64:ff9b:1::/48, and 64:ff9b::/96 (judged by embedded IPv4).
findings.code_says: fetch-citations.mjs adds six IPv6 subnets to BLOCKED (::/96, fc00::/7, fec0::/10, fe80::/10, ff00::/8, 64:ff9b:1::/48) plus the separately-checked NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 — the doc's list and count omit fc00::/7 (unique-local), fe80::/10 (link-local), and ff00::/8 (multicast), all blocked outright.

findings.doc_says: `apply-palette.mjs --swap` finds fences with `lint-mermaid.mjs`'s own `extractMermaidBlocks` and splices by its offsets, so `--block N` addresses exactly the block a finding's 1-based `block` field names
findings.code_says: apply-palette.mjs --swap takes a positional `[block]` argument (usage: `apply-palette.mjs --swap <palette.json> <file.mmd|file.md> [block]`); the `--block N` flag belongs to the separate wrapper swap-palette.sh, not apply-palette.mjs

findings.doc_says: "Three IPv6 ranges get handling beyond that" — naming only ::/96, fec0::/10, 64:ff9b:1::/48, and 64:ff9b::/96
check-prose.mjs finds: wall-of-text, dense bullets, unscannable procedures
findings.code_says: check-prose.mjs emits only WALL_OF_TEXT, DENSE_BULLET, and SPLIT_CANDIDATE (oversized file/section); no logic inspects ordered lists or procedures
